- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 7-day mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent 14-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 14-day moving average.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >2% from prior high), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day of reversion.  
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and model forecasts are rising, check for overconfidence; if forecast > 10% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overestimation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
